title: Impossible OS TODO Frontmatter
description: Canonical schema for the YAML frontmatter block carried by every file under todo/**/*.md. Mirrors docs/infrastructure/todo-metadata.md (the human-readable spec). Programmatic validators (the generator at scripts/todo-graph/build.py, CI lint via remark-lint-frontmatter-schema, ad-hoc jsonschema.validate calls) follow the per-file $schema field to load this sidecar. The stock Red Hat YAML language server does NOT auto-detect $schema as a schema directive in markdown frontmatter; editor-time diagnostics require remark-lint-frontmatter-schema or markdown-yaml-embedded-langservers. The §6 CI gate in todo/00-infrastructure/TODO-06-todo-metadata-layer.md is the authoritative line of defense.

$schema.description: Relative path to this JSON Schema file. Programmatic validators (the generator, CI lint, ad-hoc jsonschema calls) follow it. The stock Red Hat YAML language server does NOT auto-detect this as a schema directive in markdown frontmatter; editor-time diagnostics require remark-lint-frontmatter-schema or markdown-yaml-embedded-langservers. Recommended to set even though optional.

schema_version.description: Schema generation. Currently constrained to exactly 1. Bumped only on a NON-additive change (rename, removal, semantic shift); adding a new optional field does NOT bump it. The maximum tracks the current generator + schema together so editors and the generator agree on what is valid (no version-skew split brain).

id.description: Globally unique identifier across all domains. Lowercase kebab-case, 2-60 chars, must start with a letter, must not end with a dash. Stable across renumbering: renaming a TODO file does NOT change its id.

domain.description: Directory short name (folder under todo/). Matches the file's parent directory by convention but is recorded explicitly so the cache schema is self-describing.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Validator gates status: done against every Implementation Order row being [x].

title.description: Human-readable short name. May differ from the H1 heading for length reasons (the H1 is preserved for in-page display).

owners.description: Free-form list of handles, roles, or team names. NOT enforced; advisory.

depends_on.description: Structural dependencies on other TODO ids. The validator builds a digraph from this field and rejects cycles.

satisfies.description: List of ids that this TODO closes when its status flips to done. Powers auto-closure propagation in the validator (gated by full acceptance).

superseded_by.description: Single id. Set when this TODO's status is superseded. Validator surfaces a chain when traversing supersession.

file_patterns.description: Glob patterns marking source paths this TODO owns. Linux MAINTAINERS-style F: parity. Powers the code <id> query (query-CLI section).

effort.$comment: The `not` clause is load-bearing and is NOT redundant with the anchored pattern. JSON Schema does not pin a regex engine, and the two that validate this file disagree on `$`: ECMA-262 without the `m` flag anchors at end-of-input, but Python's `re` -- which jsonschema.Draft202012Validator uses, the validation path docs/infrastructure/todo-metadata.md documents -- also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so `^[1-9][0-9]*[dw]$` ACCEPTS "2w\n" there. cache_schema.EFFORT_REGEX refuses it via `\Z`, so without this clause the schema would approve a value build.py rejects, which is the exact two-layer divergence this property exists to prevent (Codex consistency review of the cache-format identity work, [medium]). An explicit CR/LF exclusion says the same thing in every engine.
effort.description: Gantt row duration read by the visualization emitter: whole days or whole weeks, e.g. '3d' or '2w'. Deliberately narrower than Mermaid's full duration grammar -- every unit this rejects is one that cannot reach the emitted gantt line, and the renderer interpolates the value directly into a row. Absent means the renderer's 1w default; a present-but-invalid value FAILS the build rather than defaulting, because a silent default hides a typo behind a plausible schedule. This property is load-bearing because additionalProperties is true here: without it, editor-time and ad-hoc jsonschema validation would approve effort values (null, 7, '4mo') that scripts/todo-graph/build.py refuses, which is precisely the two-layer split this schema exists to keep honest.

$comment: created_at, last_active_at and stamped_items are cache-only fields the generator computes (the first two from git log, the third from the per-item cache extension); they MUST NOT appear in hand-authored frontmatter. The not/anyOf clause enforces that contract at the schema layer. stamped_items was missing from the clause while scripts/todo-graph/build.py refused it, so the schema approved a TODO the generator rejects -- the two-layer split holding in one direction only.
